name: bardic order

attributes.attribute: the highest grade of the fili
panegyric and lyric poets of lower rank
feared for the power of his curse

text: The bardic order is the professional poet institution of medieval Wales and Ireland. It ranked poets by learning above raw talent. In Ireland the fili formed a fixed hierarchy of seven grades. The highest grade was the ollam. The law-tracts, such as Bretha Nemed and Uraicecht na Ríar, record the grades. The baird, or bards, held a lower place. They composed panegyric and lyric verse. Their rank turned on innate talent rather than schooled training. The fili expected a minimum three generations of poet ancestry. The satirist carried a feared curse. His word shamed a man who failed in honour.

okr.objective: Describe the ranked fili and baird institutions of the bardic order.
